newsitem.title: NORWAY: Phillips hopes for Ekofisk restart Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Phillips hopes for Ekofisk restart Thursday.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum said on Wednesday repairs were underway at the North Sea Ekofisk oilfield and it hoped to restart crude production on Thursday.
Output at ther 350,000 barrel per day (bpd) Ekofisk development was shut in early on Tuesday after a gas leak was detected in a 30 inch oil pipeline.
Oil from third party fields -- British Petroleum's Gyda and Ula and Amoco's Valhall and Hod -- and the Statpipe gas line continued to flow, Phillips spokesman Sander Bull-Gjertsen said.
"Repairs will probably take a couple of days. We anticipate to be back on stream tomorrow," he said. "It was a minor leak but enough to activate the gas alarm."
Bull-Gjertsen said it was too early to estimate the impact of the shutdown on the January schedule for Ekofisk cargoes loading at the Teeside terminal in northeast Britain.
